name: Electrical
description: Electrical and control diagrams: circuit, ladder, one-line and three-line, PLC I/O, panel, interconnection and logic, drawn to IEC 60617, IEEE 315 or JIC with IEC 81346, JIC or Y14.44 designations, cross references from contacts to coils, terminal strips and cables, and an electrical rule check.

rules.description: Each device has its own designation.
Every contact belongs to a coil: give it the coil's tag.
A coil has no more contacts drawn than it carries.
Every pin is wired.
A wire joins at least two pins.
Every wire carries a number.
Wire numbers are not repeated on different nets.
Green-yellow is kept for protective earth.
At most one wire lands on each side of a terminal.
Terminal numbers are unique on their strip.
Every interrupted line continues somewhere: two continuations share a tag.
Every cross reference names a partner that is drawn.
A rung drives one output.
The output sits at the right end of its rung.
One page uses one symbol set.
A logic net has one driver.
Every logic input is driven.
Every bus has a voltage.
Every breaker has a frame and a trip rating.
Every transformer has its rating and voltages.
A protective relay carries an IEEE C37.2 device function number.
A protective relay is fed by a current or voltage transformer.
Current transformer secondaries feed only relays and meters.
Each channel of a module is used once.
Each I/O address is used once.
A cable has two ends.
A cable's cores match its core count.
Every device is placed once on the panel layout.
